Photograph: Gilbert Flores/Variety/Getty Images Florida Florida prosecutors drop felony charge against Rick Ross in domestic violence case Miami-Dade officials drop charge of battery by strangulation against rapper due to ‘insufficient evidence’ Associated Press Fri 30 Oct 2026 14.39 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Florida prosecutors on Thursday dropped a felony charge against rapper Rick Ross nearly a month after he was arrested in Miami Beach when a woman he was living with told police he hit her, court records said. The Miami-Dade state attorney’s office filed paperwork on Thursday to drop a felony charge of battery by strangulation because of “insufficient evidence”. Ross, whose legal name is William Roberts II, still faces a misdemeanor charge of battery domestic violence. Ross, 50, has pleaded not guilty to all charges, and his attorney said on Friday that his client would continue to defend himself against the allegations. Rick Ross arrested on domestic battery and strangulation charges Read more Ross surrendered at the Miami Beach police station on 1 October, two days after the woman filed a report with police, officials said. He was freed on bail several hours later. According to an arrest report, a woman told Miami Beach detectives that she had been living with Ross when he accused her of cheating on him and struck her multiple times on 28 August. She said Ross also choked her with the collar of her shirt and slammed her into a wall. The woman said she was eventually able to leave the home and returned later – after Ross left – to collect her belongings. Ross previously pleaded no contest to aggravated assault in 2017 after he was accused of forcing a man into a guesthouse at his suburban Atlanta mansion in 2015 and beating him with a handgun, according to Georgia court records. Under a Georgia first-time offender program, the court issued an order exonerating Ross of guilt on that felony count. Ross is a longtime south Florida resident who gained prominence in 2006 with his debut single Hustlin’. The rapper and entrepreneur helped put Miami on the musical map in the early 2000s, when most hip-hop fans looked to Atlanta and Houston as the southern rap headquarters. Hustlin’ was certified platinum twice by the Recording Industry Association of America and sparked a bidding war for Ross. He eventually signed with Def Jam Records, headed by Jay-Z . Ross’s debut album, Port of Miami, also went platinum, debuting at No 1 on the Billboard 200 chart. It was the first in a series of chart-toppers, including 2008’s Trilla and 2009’s Deeper Than Rap . He has been nominated for nine Grammy awards. In 2008, he founded the Maybach Music Group label, boosting the careers of signees like Wale, Meek Mill and French Montana. His most recent album, Set In Stone, was released in July. What we know on day 1,730 Guardian staff and agencies Wed 18 Nov 2026 21.16 EST Last modified on Wed 18 Nov 2026 21.59 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Russia’s embassy in the Netherlands has posted a statement asking if the Netherlands had openly joined ⁠the conflict ⁠in ​Ukraine after a Dutch-based company said its missiles ⁠were used by Kyiv in Tuesday’s attack on a Crimean bridge . A section ​of the Kerch bridge that ‌connects annexed Crimea and Russia was destroyed on Tuesday by waves of ⁠drones and missiles. Soon after, Destinus – a Dutch-headquartered startup – confirmed its Ruta cruise missiles ‌were the only foreign-made weapons used in the attack, a rare operational role for a western manufacturer in a significant long-range strike . In response to the revelation, the ​Russian embassy said on X that “Moscow has ⁠been duly informed of the NL ( Netherlands ) involvement” , above a ​statement from ‌Destinus detailing ​its ​role in the bridge attack. The embassy added: “The confession has been well noted. Is The Hague openly joining the conflict?” In a separate strike on Wednesday, the bridge was attacked again , temporarily halting traffic. “An assessment of the damage is under way,” Sergei Aksyonov, the Moscow-appointed head of Crimea, wrote on Telegram. For Ukraine, the bridge is a hated symbol of Russian arrogance and colonial thinking. Ukraine has previously declared that the bridge across the Kerch strait, built eight years ago, is illegal. The strike came hours ahead of a meeting between Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping at Apec in China . Trump plans to meet separately with Putin on Thursday, in addition to their already scheduled three-way meeting with Xi, a US official confirmed. Trump’s meeting with Putin would be the first time that the leaders have held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year that failed to broker a deal to ease Russia’s war in Ukraine. A Russian man has been arrested in California for allegedly conducting surveillance of employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defence company that provided assistance to Ukraine , US officials said. The targeted company was not named in the indictment but it was described as a “large, publicly traded” technology and defence company with office locations throughout the US, including in Palo Alto. Ukraine struck two oil refineries in southern Russia overnight , Ukrainian officials said on Wednesday. Ukraine’s general staff said the strikes hit storage tanks at the Ilsky refinery and a processing unit at the Afipsky refinery, both in Russia’s Krasnodar region. The two refineries, also targeted Sunday night, could together process about 95m barrels of oil a year and supply Russian forces on the frontlines in southern and eastern Ukraine, it said. Russian drones attacked energy facilities, civilian businesses and residential buildings in five regions overnight and Wednesday morning , Ukrainian prime minister Serhii Koretskyi said. A Russian strike on the southern Ukrainian city of Odesa killed four people, officials said. A Russian drone attack on a market in the Kharkiv region wounded 12 people, including an 11-year-old boy, Ukraine’s State Emergency Services said. The EU has proposed member states give Ukraine an extra €45bn ($49bn) loan to plug its 2027 budget shortfalls as Russia’s invasion drags on , Jennifer Rankin writes . The funding would fill two-thirds of a €70bn black hole Kyiv faces next year. “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiation table, and Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine,” European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said. EU leaders will discuss the loan next week. US diplomatic envoys Steve Witkoff and ⁠Jared Kushner are expected in Berlin on Thursday to meet Ukrainian officials and a European negotiating team , a US official said. The meetings would focus on further developing “credible postwar security guarantees” ⁠for Ukraine, and preparing for the next round of multilateral talks, the official said. Russian ⁠athletes will not be allowed into ⁠the ⁠Czech Republic, ​which is hosting ⁠the women’s under-18 ice hockey world championship ⁠in January. In comments to local media, interior minister ‌Lubomir Metnar ‌reiterated his government would not ‌be issuing visas for Russian ​athletes. He added that the ministry also had ⁠legal instruments to ​prevent entry for ​athletes ​receiving visas from ​other ‌states ​in ​Europe’s border-free Schengen zone.
